purpose: Targeted development diagnostic: fresh wording of known tasks, not held-out information needs.
review: Single-author question/source review before rankings; no independent reviewer claim. Original assertions retained; known alternate version source added before results.

cases.query: Our nightly test must keep using the wording we published last Friday even when teammates publish edits under the same prompt name. How can we retrieve that particular revision reliably?

nuggets.description: Publishing changed content under the same name creates a new immutable version and preserves older versions.

acceptable_passages.quote: Each version is immutable. Once created, the contents of that version cannot be changed. If you update a prompt and publish it again, Weave creates a new version while preserving previous versions.

nuggets.description: Load a chosen prompt version with weave.ref(name:version).get(), rather than the unqualified latest version.

acceptable_passages.quote:
* `weave.ref(<name>)`: Retrieves the `:latest` version of a prompt. Requires calling `weave.init(...)`.
* `weave.ref(<name>:<alias_or_version>)`: Retrieves a prompt by alias, version hash, or version index. Requires calling `weave.init(...)`.

assertions.description: Explains that publishing changed prompt content creates a new immutable version while preserving the old version.
Describes loading a specific stored version through a reference and .get(), instead of relying on an unqualified name that resolves to latest.

cases.query: I changed both my assistant's instructions and its model settings. How do I keep those app revisions identifiable in Weave and inspect which individual test answers improved or regressed?

nuggets.description: A Weave Model tracks application code and parameters; changes produce versions that can be compared.

acceptable_passages.quote:
When you change the parameters or the code that defines your model, Weave logs these changes and updates the version.
This lets you compare predictions across versions of your model. Use this to iterate on prompts or to try a different LLM and compare predictions across settings.

This guide shows you how to define a Weave `Model`, call it to capture inputs and outputs, take advantage of automatic versioning when your code or parameters change, serve the model behind a local API, and tag production calls for filtering.

The system prompt, the tools, the control flow, and the underlying LLM are all considered part of the model version. To compare two versions, run the evaluation again on the changed agent, labeled as a new version.

nuggets.description: Use Dataset results for per-example outputs and scorer metrics across evaluations.

acceptable_passages.quote: Select **Dataset results** to compare individual dataset examples across the selected evaluations. Each row corresponds to one dataset example and shows the dataset input alongside each evaluation's output and scorer metrics, so you can inspect where a specific example diverges. Select a row to open a side-by-side detail view.

assertions.description: Describes a documented way to track the app code and configuration as separate versions, such as Weave Model versioning.
Directs the user to per-example evaluation comparisons to inspect outputs and scorer metrics, rather than claiming aggregate scores show every regression.

cases.query: The pictures are already in S3, bucket permissions and CORS are set, and I trace both regular Python functions and an agent's tools. What setup remains, and what should each path record to display those pictures in Weave?

nuggets.description: Register the reference bucket in team settings before expecting rendering.

acceptable_passages.quote: Until the bucket is registered, referenced URIs do not render. Registration is what lets Weave presign and display the object.
Until the bucket is registered, referenced URIs do not render. Registration is what lets Weave presign and display the object.

nuggets.description: For an Op, a bucket URI in a string input or output can render in the trace without a content annotation.

acceptable_passages.quote: Log the URI as a string value in a trace. Any string field whose value is a bucket URI renders. No content annotation is needed because the bytes stay in your bucket.

nuggets.description: For an agent, return the URI as a tool result so it renders on that tool call in the Agents view.

acceptable_passages.quote: Return a bucket URI as an agent tool result and Weave renders it inline in the **Agents** view, on the tool call that produced it.

assertions.description: Describes registering the bucket as a team reference bucket before rendering will work.
Describes logging a bucket URI string in an Op input/output and returning the URI as an agent tool result.
Keeps the existing image bytes in the bucket and distinguishes the ordinary Traces path from the Agents path.

nuggets.description: Log the object URI; media bytes remain in the existing bucket.

acceptable_passages.quote: Instead of re-uploading those bytes into Weave, you log the object's URI as a string and Weave renders the image or video inline from your bucket. Only the URI is sent to Weave; the bytes stay in your bucket.

Instead of re-uploading those bytes into Weave, you log the object's URI as a string and Weave renders the image or video inline from your bucket. Only the URI is sent to Weave; the bytes stay in your bucket.

nuggets.description: Configure bucket read access and browser CORS for reference rendering.

acceptable_passages.quote: Grant W\&B read access to the bucket and allow the browser to fetch objects with CORS.
Grant W\&B read access to the bucket and allow the browser to fetch objects with CORS.

nuggets.description: Register the reference bucket in team settings before expecting rendering.

acceptable_passages.quote: Until the bucket is registered, referenced URIs do not render. Registration is what lets Weave presign and display the object.
Until the bucket is registered, referenced URIs do not render. Registration is what lets Weave presign and display the object.

cases.query: I am adding postprocess_inputs and postprocess_output to a Python @weave.op. What types go into and out of each hook, and which representation is saved in the trace?

nuggets.description: Use Op postprocessing hooks to transform logged data without changing the original function.

acceptable_passages.quote: To change the data that Weave logs without modifying the original function (for example, to hide sensitive data), pass `postprocess_inputs` and `postprocess_output` to the Op decorator.

nuggets.description: The input hook receives and returns a dictionary of argument names to values.

acceptable_passages.quote: `postprocess_inputs` takes a dict where the keys are the argument names and the values are the argument values, and returns a dict with the transformed inputs.

nuggets.description: The output hook receives the normal return value and returns its transformed logged representation.

acceptable_passages.quote: `postprocess_output` takes any value that the function would normally return and returns the transformed output.

assertions.description: Correctly identifies postprocess_inputs as receiving and returning an argument-name/value dictionary.
Correctly identifies postprocess_output as receiving the original return value and returning its transformed logged representation.
Explains that the hooks customize the data recorded by the Python Op.

cases.query: For one op_name, how do I request a daily total cost and mean latency from POST /calls/stats? Explain granularity and the usage_metrics and call_metrics fields.

nuggets.description: Use POST /calls/stats for aggregate Call metrics without retrieving underlying Call records.

acceptable_passages.quote: You can also use the Weave Service API's [POST `/calls/stats` endpoint](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/reference/service-api/calls/call-stats) to retrieve metrics about your Calls without retrieving the Call data itself.

nuggets.description: Set granularity in seconds to choose the time-bucket size, such as 86400 for daily buckets.

acceptable_passages.quote:
# Specify the size of the buckets, in seconds.
    "granularity": 86400,

nuggets.description: Select the Op and request total cost plus average latency using the documented filter and metric fields.

assertions.description: Uses POST /calls/stats with a daily granularity in seconds and the documented Op-name filter.
Uses total_cost with sum under usage_metrics and latency_ms with avg under call_metrics if giving a request example.
